package_info.package_name: AgentTesla Christmas Campaign / Die Hard-themed Batch+PowerShell Dropper
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing email attachments, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious executables and scripts, not versioned packages)
package_info.why_malicious: The campaign delivers malware via phishing emails with holiday themes, using malicious executables and scripts to open backdoors, exfiltrate credentials, and enable remote control of infected systems. The payloads include AgentTesla infostealer and a batch file that downloads and executes a PowerShell-based reverse shell.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Upon execution, drops fkkvzetzm.exe, jfwxswcu.au3, igqyivch.prc, and kywyozha.x into %usertemp%, then launches fkkvzetzm.exe (AutoIt3) with jfwxswcu.au3 as argument.
malicious_snippets.code_language: Windows executable (drops AutoIt script and binaries)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At user-execution, the code drops multiple files to the temp directory and launches an obfuscated AutoIt script, setting up a multi-stage malware loader.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping and executing multiple files, especially obfuscated scripts, is a common malware staging technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal executables from legitimate sources do not drop and execute obfuscated scripts or additional binaries in temp directories.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software installers may unpack files, but not obfuscated scripts or unknown binaries to temp.
key_indicators: Obfuscated AutoIt script dropped and executed
Multiple files with random names dropped to temp
Execution chain designed to evade detection

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated AutoIt script reads and deobfuscates igqyivch.prc (shellcode), allocates memory via VirtualAlloc, loads shellcode, which then loads kywyozha.x into memory.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script deobfuscates and loads shellcode into memory, which then loads an additional executable payload, enabling in-memory execution and evasion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: In-memory loading of shellcode and executables is a hallmark of advanced malware seeking to evade disk-based detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate AutoIt scripts do not load and execute shellcode or additional binaries from obfuscated sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing frameworks may use similar techniques for red teaming.
key_indicators: Obfuscated script deobfuscating and executing shellcode
Use of VirtualAlloc for memory execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Shellcode loads kywyozha.x into memory, launches a copy of the running process, checks for 64bit process, copies ntdll.dll into memory, checks for API hooks, and injects kywyozha.x into the new process.
malicious_snippets.code_language: Shellcode (x86/x64 assembly, executed via AutoIt loader)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the shellcode loads and injects the main payload into a new process, performs anti-analysis checks, and uses in-memory copies of system DLLs to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process injection, anti-analysis, and in-memory DLL loading are advanced evasion and persistence techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not inject code into other processes or copy system DLLs into memory for stealth.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security tools or debuggers may use process injection for analysis.
key_indicators: In-memory DLL copy and API hook checks

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: AgentTesla infostealer variant: downloads/deletes files, steals credentials from browsers, FTP, email apps, performs keylogging, communicates with C2 via Telegram API (hxxps://api.telegram[.]org/bot5018340186:AAFKw8ktzY7O_6e1fhgEWq27H2aE-rsBGjA/).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload exfiltrates credentials and keystrokes, enables remote file operations, and communicates with a Telegram-based C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credential theft, keylogging, and C2 communication are core infostealer behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not exfiltrate credentials or communicate with Telegram C2 servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools may have similar capabilities, but with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Batch file displays image7.jpg.jpg and loads/executes PowerShell code from hxxps://pastebin[.]com/raw/PeJLUFC4.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At user-execution, the batch file masquerades as an image, displays a decoy, and downloads and executes a remote PowerShell script.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Batch files disguised as images that download and execute remote scripts are a classic malware delivery method.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Image files should not contain executable code or download scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT automation may use batch files to run scripts, but not disguised as images.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PowerShell script creates a reverse shell backdoor, allowing execution of arbitrary PowerShell commands from the attacker's system.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script establishes a reverse shell, enabling the attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reverse shells are a primary method for attackers to gain remote control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PowerShell scripts should not create unauthorized remote access channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Red teamers and sysadmins may use reverse shells for testing or remote support, but not via disguised image files.

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious attachment (holiday-themed).
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens attachment, triggering malware execution.

attack_chain.action: User executes malicious file (either .exe or disguised batch file).
Malware loader drops and executes obfuscated scripts and shellcode (AgentTesla chain) or downloads and runs PowerShell (Die Hard chain).
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is loaded into memory or reverse shell is established.

attack_chain.action: Payload executes: AgentTesla infostealer exfiltrates data and communicates with C2, or PowerShell reverse shell gives attacker remote access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration, remote control, and further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Executable or script drops multiple files with random names to temp directories
Obfuscated AutoIt scripts that deobfuscate and execute shellcode
In-memory loading of executables and DLLs
Process injection and anti-analysis checks (API hook detection, ntdll.dll in-memory copy)
Batch files disguised as images that download and execute PowerShell scripts
file_indicators: Files with random names in %usertemp% (e.g., fkkvzetzm.exe, jfwxswcu.au3, igqyivch.prc, kywyozha.x)
Archives containing executables or disguised batch files (e.g., good_time.zip, new designs.gz)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of files with suspicious or double extensions (e.g., .jpg.bat), especially from email attachments. Detect batch files or scripts that download and execute remote PowerShell code. Flag in-memory execution of shellcode, process injection, and use of obfuscated AutoIt scripts. Watch for outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure (Telegram API, pastebin links). Alert on credential access, keylogging, and attempts to exfiltrate data via unusual network channels.
